text:
Luke Hughes spent last season as the defenseman with the skating everyone talks about and the defensive numbers nobody wanted to discuss. Sixteen games into this one, he is the reason people are asking whether New Jersey got a bargain. The Hockey News used him as its example of the reward for paying defensemen with upside, and he has six goals already, the same total he had in 68 games last year. He is playing almost 24 and a half minutes a night, and the Devils are winning the 5v5 shot battle by a wide margin when he is out there.

Now the honest part. Those six goals came on about three goals' worth of chances (expected goals measure the quality of a shooter's looks), and he is shooting 15% after 4% last season. The chances themselves are up, which is real progress, but the finishing will cool. Our projection still has him around 48 points. What we would watch is his own end: Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting noticeably more with him on the ice in 2025-26, near the bottom of the league's defensemen. If that number moves, this is a leap and not a hot month.
headline: Luke Hughes is scoring like a forward
